text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a regression on 4xA100 TP runs after the kernel-picker change on Monday. P95 tokens/sec down ~12% and we're seeing transient GPU mem spikes that push a few long-chat sessions to OOM.

chris: Hmm, did you correlate with sequence length distribution or batching changes?

maria: seq_len skewed toward 2048 in the repro traffic. Batching heuristics didn't change for this load. profiler shows a new workspace choice for the attention kernel that allocates a ~1.6GB temp buffer per shard at certain seq/batch combos.

lin: Can you paste the profiler sample and repro command?

maria: repro command: ```bash
pytest tests/integration/tp_mem.py::test_long_chat --gpus=4 --batch=1 --seq=2048
```
profiler snippet: ```
# extracted from runtime trace at kernel-picker v2.3.1
gpu0: kv_cache_shadow: +512MB
gpu0: attention_ws_alloc: 1.6GB
gpu0: comm_temp_per_stream: 192MB
aggregate transient ~= 2.3GB per GPU
```

alan: That attention_ws sounds like the fused kernel that trades extra workspace for fewer kernels. We enabled it to improve latency for short sequences, but for long sequences + TP this blows up.

rachel: We saw something similar in canary but thought it was traffic skew. Good catch. Any quick mitigations?

maria: Two options: 1) revert kernel-picker change, 2) change heuristic to add workspace_penalty and require comm_headroom on TP runs so fused kernel isn't picked when kv_cache + comm buffers exceed threshold. I prototyped #2 and reduced peak transient by ~40% in local runs.

chris: Patch idea?

maria: Patch diff (conceptual): ```python
def score_kernel(k):
    est_ws = k.estimate_workspace(seq_len, batch)
    comm_headroom = cluster_config.get('tp_comm_headroom_bytes', 512*1024*1024)
    kv_shadow = estimator.kv_cache_shadow_bytes(batch, seq_len)
    penalty = max(0, est_ws + kv_shadow + comm_headroom - gpu_free_estimate())
    return base_score - penalty_weight * penalty
```

lin: Nice. Also consider reusing comm buffers across streams instead of per-stream temp allocs — that was a big win in 2-GPU tests.

maria: Yep I toggled shared_comm_pool in runtime and saw per-GPU transient drop by ~200MB. Not enough alone.

devops-bot: deploybot: staging deploy of runtime/kernel-picker v2.3.2 started by maria at 2087654380

alan: Can we add a safety fallback: if memory estimate + margin > free then pick low-memory kernel and log an event to tracing?

maria: Doing that now. Also adding a metric "kernel_picker.fallback.low_memory" so we can alert when it happens frequently.

rachel: For the KV cache growth — is it actual retention or shadow bookkeeping?

maria: It's shadow buffers we allocate for async eviction. I trimmed retention window and added pooling for shadow bufs in my branch. Local: shadow peak -45%.

sre-bot: incidentbot: started a temporary alert for p95 token throughput drop in eng-runtime — threshold 10% sustained for 5m

chris: Great. Next steps: (1) land kernel-picker heuristic with fallback + metric, (2) enable shared_comm_pool for TP clusters behind a flag, (3) KV shadow pooling + retention trim, (4) run a 24h soak on staging with seq skewed to 2k.

alan: I'll own the soak and perf numbers. maria, can you post before/after perf table once patched?

maria: Will do. Quick numbers from local patch: baseline P95 tokens/sec 1280 -> patched 1408 (rough numbers because fallback avoided fused kernel for long seq). Peak transient per GPU: 3.1GB -> 1.9GB.

lin: Sweet. If that holds on staging we can roll to dedicated clusters with a config toggle.

rachel: Thanks for the fast triage. :thumbsup:

maria: filing a follow-up PR and test plan. linking to trace: https://internal-redwood/traces/2087654321-kernel-picker-regression

chris: Ping me on the PR for quick review.

maria: will do.
